record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: If a morphism f generates a quasiperiodic infinite word and f(a) is not a power of a, must f be weakly quasiperiodic on every infinite word?

evidence.quote: Let f be an morphism generating a quasiperiodic infinite word. If f (a) is not a power of a then f is weakly quasiperiodic on any infinite word. The authors deﬁneweakly quasiperiodic morphisms as those that map at least one non-quasiperiodic word to a quasiperiodic one (some partial answers are given in the paper).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a finite alphabet and $A^*$ (resp. $A^\omega$) the set of finite (resp. right-infinite) words over $A$. A morphism is a map $f: A^* \to A^*$ satisfying $f(uv) = f(u)f(v)$ for all $u, v \in A^*$; it extends naturally to $A^\omega$ when $|f^n(a)| \to \infty$ for some letter $a$.

An infinite word $w \in A^\omega$ is said to be quasiperiodic if there exists a finite word $q$ (a quasiperiod) such that every position of $w$ lies inside an occurrence of $q$ in $w$; equivalently, $w$ can be written as an overlapping concatenation of occurrences of $q$. A morphism $f$ is called weakly quasiperiodic if there exists at least one non-quasiperiodic infinite word $w \in A^\omega$ such that $f(w)$ is quasiperiodic.

Suppose that $f: A^* \to A^*$ is a morphism such that, for some letter $a \in A$, the infinite word $f^\omega(a) = \lim_{n \to \infty} f^n(a)$ is well-defined and quasiperiodic, and such that $f(a)$ is not a power of $a$ (i.e., $f(a) \notin \{a^k : k \geq 0\}$).

Prove or disprove: under these hypotheses, $f$ must be weakly quasiperiodic on every infinite word, in the sense that for every non-quasiperiodic infinite word $w \in A^\omega$, the image $f(w)$ is quasiperiodic.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches surface foundational work on (weakly/strongly) quasiperiodic morphisms by Levé and Richomme and related papers on quasiperiodic Sturmian words, but none of the readily available sources explicitly resolve the stated implication in full generality. Partial answers exist in the original framework, but no definitive proof or counterexample for the general conjecture was located.

status_evidence.title: Quasiperiodic Sturmian words and morphisms
status_evidence.snippet: Weakly and strongly quasiperiodic morphisms are tools introduced to study quasiperiodic words, formally mapping respectively at least one or any non-quasiperiodic word to a quasiperiodic word.
status_evidence.claim: Defines weakly quasiperiodic morphisms; partial results known but the general conjecture is not stated as resolved.

status_evidence.title: Quasiperiods of biinfinite Sturmian words
status_evidence.snippet: Studies quasiperiods of Sturmian biinfinite words, extending earlier work on quasiperiodic morphisms.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work continues to explore quasiperiodic morphism properties without resolving the general implication.
